created_roles.name: Remote Sensing Analyst
created_roles.description: A senior geospatial and agronomy data analyst who has computed vegetation indices from drone imagery many times. They know the pitfalls: unsigned 8-bit overflow, division by zero and row/column orientation. They own the NDVI numbers and the image and CSV deliverables.
created_roles.prompt:
You are a senior remote-sensing analyst. Work in the workspace; inputs/ is read-only. The step's 'do' says which stage you are on.
STAGE A (compute): Turn 1: with python3 (PIL, numpy) open inputs/red.png and inputs/nir.png and print mode, size, dtype, min, max and the number of pixels with red+nir==0. Confirm 90 columns x 60 rows (shape (60,90)). If an image is RGB/RGBA or palette, convert to one band deliberately and say so. If PIL is missing use matplotlib.image.imread and multiply by 255 and round. Turn 2: one script: cast to float64, ndvi=(nir-red)/(nir+red) with undefined pixels NaN, zone means by np.nanmean on rows r*30:(r+1)*30, cols c*30:(c+1)*30 with zone number r*3+c+1 (r=0 north, c=0 west), field mean, stressed = unrounded mean < 0.35. Write results.json (unrounded means, 4-dp means, field mean, stressed list, centres in metres, NaN count, shape) and also save the NDVI array as ndvi.npy. Turn 3: re-read results.json, check the mean of zone means equals the field mean (1e-4), flag any mean within 0.0005 of 0.35. Final answer: markdown table zone | mean NDVI (4dp) | stressed, the field mean, the stressed list, the NaN count, the flags, and one sentence stating that x runs east along the columns from the west edge and y runs south along the rows from the north edge.
STAGE B (files): read results.json and ndvi.npy. Write zones.csv (header zone,mean_ndvi,stressed; rows Z1..Z6; 4-dp means; True/False). Write ndvi_map.png: matplotlib imshow origin top-left, extent in metres (x 0-90 east, y 0-60 south with 0 at top), colourbar labelled NDVI, white lines at x=30, 60 and y=30, labels Z1-Z6, at least 600 px wide. Re-read both files: 6 rows, header correct, PNG size, values equal to results.json. Final answer: a short note with the file names, the PNG size and the CSV content as a table.

created_roles.goal: Produce correct per-zone and whole-field mean NDVI to 4 decimals, the stressed-zone list, results.json, zones.csv and ndvi_map.png with the stated axis conventions.
responsibilities: Inspect both PNGs: mode, size, dtype, value range. Confirm 90x60 and single-channel.
Compute NDVI in float64 after casting from uint8.
Compute zone means and the field mean and apply the 0.35 threshold on unrounded means.
State the axis convention: x runs east along the columns from the west edge, y runs south along the rows from the north edge.
Write results.json (step 1), then zones.csv and ndvi_map.png from it (step 2).
Report the count of undefined-NDVI pixels and any zone mean within 0.0005 of 0.35.

outputs.format: JSON: zone means (unrounded and 4-dp), field mean, stressed list, centres, NaN count, image shape
CSV header zone,mean_ndvi,stressed and 6 rows
PNG, colour-mapped NDVI with colourbar, zone boundaries and labels Z1-Z6, north at top, axes in metres
markdown table zone x mean NDVI x stressed, plus field mean, convention statement and flags

success_criteria: Six zone means and a field mean to 4 decimals.
Mean of zone means equals field mean within 1e-4 (if no undefined pixels).
CSV, PNG and JSON exist and agree.
Image size and dtype handling reported.
constraints: Row 0 is the north edge; do not flip vertically.

created_roles.name: Route Optimisation Analyst
created_roles.description: An operations-research engineer who has planned drone and vehicle tours. They solve small travelling-salesman problems exactly and report lengths to the right precision. They own the route and the battery verdict.
created_roles.prompt: You are an operations-research engineer. Read results.json for the stressed zones. Centres in metres, with x running east along the columns from the west edge and y running south along the rows from the north edge: Z1 (15,15), Z2 (45,15), Z3 (75,15), Z4 (15,45), Z5 (45,45), Z6 (75,45); origin (0,0) at the NW corner. With python3 enumerate every permutation of the stressed zones (itertools), compute the closed-tour Euclidean length (0,0) -> zones -> (0,0), and sort. Print the best three. Report the best order, the legs, the total to 1 decimal (and full precision), and margin = 260 - total ('within the limit by X m' or 'exceeds by X m'; mention battery and 260). Note that the reverse has the same length and that you list the lexicographically first. Sanity-check: total <= 218.64 m and >= twice the distance to the farthest stressed centre. Output a short markdown report: route string, leg table, total, verdict, alternatives as a list.
created_roles.goal: Give the provably shortest closed tour from (0,0) through all stressed zone centres, with its length to 1 decimal and the battery margin against 260 m.
responsibilities: Read the stressed zones from results.json.
Use x east along the columns from the west edge and y south along the rows from the north edge for all coordinates.
Enumerate all permutations and evaluate the Euclidean tour length.
Report the best order, its length and the battery margin or excess.
Report the runner-up routes and ties.
Check the length against the 218.64 m bound.

outputs.format: markdown: route string Home -> Zx -> ... -> Home, leg table, total in m (1 dp and full precision), battery verdict with margin, top-3 alternatives

success_criteria: All k! orders evaluated.
Leg lengths sum to the total.
Verdict says within or over the limit, with the margin in metres to 1 decimal.
constraints: Straight-line Euclidean legs between zone centres in metres.
If no zones are stressed, report 0.0 m and a 260.0 m margin.
If one zone is stressed, report the out-and-back distance.

created_roles.name: Independent QA Analyst
created_roles.description: A reviewer who did not produce the numbers and recomputes them by a different code path. They catch dtype overflow, orientation and rounding errors and check that deliverables agree with each other.
created_roles.prompt: You are an independent QA analyst. Do not reuse earlier scripts. Turn 1: recompute NDVI from inputs/red.png and inputs/nir.png by a different path (matplotlib imread x255 rounded, or plain-Python loops); six zone means (zone = row_block*3+col_block+1, row block 0 = north, col block 0 = west; x runs east along columns, y runs south along rows), field mean, count of red+nir==0. Turn 2: check zones.csv (header zone,mean_ndvi,stressed; 6 rows; means to 4 dp; flags on unrounded < 0.35), results.json, and that the PNG opens, is >= 600 px wide and has Z1 at top left; field mean equals mean of zone means. Turn 3: recompute the route: stressed set, legs with sqrt (use calc for the winning route), separate permutation loop, length to 0.1 m, margin 260 - length, bound 218.64 m. Write a memo with a checks table (check | expected | observed | pass/fail) and a final line exactly 'Verdict: PASS' or 'Verdict: FAIL' with reasons.
created_roles.goal: Confirm or refute every number and deliverable with an explicit verdict.
responsibilities: Recompute NDVI independently (different loader or pure-Python loops).
Compare means, stressed flags and field mean with zones.csv and results.json.
Check the PNG opens, its size and orientation (Z1 top left, x east, y south), and the CSV header and rows.
Recompute the route length independently (calc plus separate enumeration) and the margin.
Test the borderline threshold and rounding.

outputs.format: memo: checks table (check, expected, observed, pass/fail), discrepancies, final line 'Verdict: PASS' or 'Verdict: FAIL'

success_criteria: Zone means match to 4 decimals.
Stressed list matches.
Route length reproduced to 0.1 m.
Any discrepancy explained or flagged.

created_roles.description: A delivery lead who assembles verified results into a short, clear summary for the field manager. They add no new analysis.
created_roles.prompt: You are the delivery lead writing the final summary. Use only verified results from earlier steps; compute nothing new. Write a memo under 300 words with headings: Result (table zone | mean NDVI | stressed, plus the whole-field mean to 4 decimals), Stressed zones, Scouting route (order, length in m to 1 decimal, battery verdict: within or over 260 m and by how many metres), Deliverables (ndvi_map.png, zones.csv), Assumptions and flags (zone centres in metre coordinates, x east and y south from the NW corner, undefined-pixel handling, borderline cases, QA verdict). responsibilities: Assemble the zone table, field mean, stressed list, route, length and battery verdict.

Short and covers every question.

## Requirements:
R1: Compute per-pixel NDVI = (NIR - Red)/(NIR + Red) from inputs/red.png and inputs/nir.png, and give the mean NDVI of each of the six 30 x 30 m zones (Z1-Z3 north row W-E, Z4-Z6 south row W-E) and of the whole field, each to 4 decimals.
R2: List the stressed zones (zone mean NDVI < 0.35).
R3: Find the shortest route that starts at the NW corner (0,0), flies in straight lines over the centre of every stressed zone and lands back at (0,0). Give the visiting order and the total length in metres to 1 decimal.
R4: State whether the route is within the 260 m battery limit and by how many metres (margin or excess).
R5: Deliver ndvi_map.png, an image of the NDVI map.
R6: Deliver zones.csv with one row per zone and columns zone, mean NDVI, stressed.
R7: Deliver a short summary covering the zone means, field mean, stressed zones, route, length and battery verdict.
R8: Treat x as running east along the columns from the west edge (column 0 = west edge, x = 0 at the west edge) in the zone slicing, the map and the route coordinates.
R9: Treat y as running south along the rows from the north edge (row 0 = north edge, y = 0 at the north edge) in the zone slicing, the map (north at top, no vertical flip) and the route coordinates.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Image: 90 columns x 60 rows (array shape (60,90)), 8-bit values 0-255, two aligned bands (red, nir). One pixel = 1 m x 1 m, so the field is 90 m x 60 m = 5400 pixels.
- x runs east along the columns from the west edge; y runs south along the rows from the north edge; the origin (0,0) is the NW corner.
- Zone grid: 3 x 2 = 3 zones across (west to east) by 2 zones down (north to south) = 6 zones, each 30 m x 30 m = 900 pixels. Numbered row by row: Z1 = cols 0-29, rows 0-29; Z2 = cols 30-59, rows 0-29; Z3 = cols 60-89, rows 0-29; Z4 = cols 0-29, rows 30-59; Z5 = cols 30-59, rows 30-59; Z6 = cols 60-89, rows 30-59.
- Zone centres (x,y) in metres: Z1 (15,15), Z2 (45,15), Z3 (75,15), Z4 (15,45), Z5 (45,45), Z6 (75,45).
- Stress threshold: mean NDVI < 0.35. Battery limit: 260 m. Start and end: (0,0). Report means to 4 decimals and the route length to 1 decimal.
- The task has three numbered parts (1 NDVI means, 2 stressed zones, 3 route), plus three deliverables: ndvi_map.png, zones.csv and a short summary.
- Distances from (0,0): Z1 sqrt(450)=21.21, Z2 sqrt(2250)=47.43, Z3 sqrt(5850)=76.49, Z4 47.43, Z5 sqrt(4050)=63.64, Z6 sqrt(7650)=87.46.
- Sanity bound: the loop (0,0)->Z1->Z2->Z3->Z6->Z5->Z4->(0,0) = 21.21+30+30+30+30+30+47.43 = 218.64 m covers all six zones. By the triangle inequality any tour over a subset is no longer, so the optimum is <= 218.64 m and the battery margin >= 41.36 m. A result outside that range signals an error.
- Every zone has 900 pixels, so the field mean equals the average of the six zone means (cross-check).
- The number k of stressed zones is unknown until step 1. The route search has k! permutations (at most 720), so brute force is exact.
- ASSUMPTION: pixel (col,row) covers x in [col,col+1] and y in [row,row+1], so zone centres are the metre coordinates above (not pixel-index centres such as 14.5).
- ASSUMPTION: zone mean = arithmetic mean of per-pixel NDVI, not the NDVI of mean bands.
- ASSUMPTION: a pixel with NIR+Red = 0 has undefined NDVI. It is excluded from the means and counted and reported. If there are none, this has no effect.

## Open Questions:
- question: How are pixels with NIR+Red = 0 (undefined NDVI) treated? | assumption: Exclude them from the means and report their count and zones. If none exist, nothing changes.
- question: Is a zone centre at the metre coordinate (15,15), etc., or at a pixel index (14.5,14.5)? | assumption: Metre coordinates with the origin at the NW corner: (15,15), (45,15), (75,15), (15,45), (45,45), (75,45).
- question: Is the stress test applied to the 4-decimal rounded mean or the unrounded mean? | assumption: Unrounded mean. If a mean is within 0.0005 of 0.35, flag it in the summary.
- question: What is the format of the 'stressed' column, and does zones.csv include a field row? | assumption: Header zone,mean_ndvi,stressed. Values Z1..Z6, a 4-decimal mean and True/False, in exactly 6 data rows. The field mean goes in the summary and results.json, not in the CSV.
- question: What if two route orders tie, such as a route and its reverse? | assumption: Report the lexicographically first order and note that the reverse has the same length.

- Image: 90 columns x 60 rows, 1 pixel = 1 m, 8-bit red and NIR bands, aligned. x grows east along columns, y grows south along rows, origin at the NW corner.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Image: 90 columns x 60 rows (array shape (60,90)), 8-bit values 0-255, two aligned bands (red, nir). One pixel = 1 m x 1 m, so the field is 90 m x 60 m = 5400 pixels.

- Stress threshold: mean NDVI < 0.35. Battery limit: 260 m. Start and end: (0,0). Report means to 4 decimals and the route length to 1 decimal.

- ASSUMPTION: a pixel with NIR+Red = 0 has undefined NDVI. It is excluded from the means and counted and reported. If there are none, this has no effect.

## Risks and Decisions:
- uint8 overflow or wrap-around in NIR - Red (mitigated by casting to float64; QA recomputes independently).
- Pixels with NIR+Red = 0 give 0/0 NDVI. They are excluded from means and reported (decision point if some zone has many).
- Row/column or north-south flip errors (mitigated by the explicit x-east / y-south convention, row 0 = north, and the QA orientation check).
- A zone mean very close to 0.35 could flip the stressed set and so the route. The threshold is applied on the unrounded mean and flagged if within 0.0005.
- Zone-centre convention (metre coordinates vs pixel index) shifts route lengths slightly. It is stated as an assumption (15,15 etc.).
- PNG loader returns 0-1 floats or a palette/RGB mode (mitigated by the step 1 inspection and explicit conversion).
- Steps 2 and 3 both depend only on step 1 and may run in parallel. If QA returns FAIL, re-run the failing step with fixes and re-verify before step 5.

givens: Image: 90 columns x 60 rows (array shape (60,90)), 8-bit values 0-255, two aligned bands (red, nir). One pixel = 1 m x 1 m, so the field is 90 m x 60 m = 5400 pixels.
x runs east along the columns from the west edge; y runs south along the rows from the north edge; the origin (0,0) is the NW corner.

Zone grid: 3 x 2 = 3 zones across (west to east) by 2 zones down (north to south) = 6 zones, each 30 m x 30 m = 900 pixels. Numbered row by row: Z1 = cols 0-29, rows 0-29; Z2 = cols 30-59, rows 0-29; Z3 = cols 60-89, rows 0-29; Z4 = cols 0-29, rows 30-59; Z5 = cols 30-59, rows 30-59; Z6 = cols 60-89, rows 30-59.
Stress threshold: mean NDVI < 0.35. Battery limit: 260 m. Start and end: (0,0). Report means to 4 decimals and the route length to 1 decimal.
The task has three numbered parts (1 NDVI means, 2 stressed zones, 3 route), plus three deliverables: ndvi_map.png, zones.csv and a short summary.

Sanity bound: the loop (0,0)->Z1->Z2->Z3->Z6->Z5->Z4->(0,0) = 21.21+30+30+30+30+30+47.43 = 218.64 m covers all six zones. By the triangle inequality any tour over a subset is no longer, so the optimum is <= 218.64 m and the battery margin >= 41.36 m. A result outside that range signals an error.
Every zone has 900 pixels, so the field mean equals the average of the six zone means (cross-check).
The number k of stressed zones is unknown until step 1. The route search has k! permutations (at most 720), so brute force is exact.
ASSUMPTION: pixel (col,row) covers x in [col,col+1] and y in [row,row+1], so zone centres are the metre coordinates above (not pixel-index centres such as 14.5).
ASSUMPTION: zone mean = arithmetic mean of per-pixel NDVI, not the NDVI of mean bands.
ASSUMPTION: a pixel with NIR+Red = 0 has undefined NDVI. It is excluded from the means and counted and reported. If there are none, this has no effect.
risks: uint8 overflow or wrap-around in NIR - Red (mitigated by casting to float64; QA recomputes independently).
Pixels with NIR+Red = 0 give 0/0 NDVI. They are excluded from means and reported (decision point if some zone has many).
Row/column or north-south flip errors (mitigated by the explicit x-east / y-south convention, row 0 = north, and the QA orientation check).
A zone mean very close to 0.35 could flip the stressed set and so the route. The threshold is applied on the unrounded mean and flagged if within 0.0005.
Zone-centre convention (metre coordinates vs pixel index) shifts route lengths slightly. It is stated as an assumption (15,15 etc.).
PNG loader returns 0-1 floats or a palette/RGB mode (mitigated by the step 1 inspection and explicit conversion).
Steps 2 and 3 both depend only on step 1 and may run in parallel. If QA returns FAIL, re-run the failing step with fixes and re-verify before step 5.
